This is a double-edged sword as the Pursuit was way more consistent than the Ace Pilot, but fast enemies often just walked right past it. It also had the same placement limit, being 10. Anyways, as for the stats, it was quite cheap for the DPS it dealt, though the DPS was hampered quite a lot by the ROF bug though. It can also deal splash damage at Level 2+, though the missiles have a mediocre damage and explosion radius, so they weren't really useful, but it does make the tower a better counter to shielded enemies, as it also fires fast. matches.title: DPS Could Be Misleading, What’s Better?
matches.snippet: We repeatedly seeing questions / polls to compare towers. Most typically Commander vs DJ, Minigunner vs Turret, Enforcer vs John, etc. Most people use DPS (damage per second) as an indicator. E.g. DPS of Golden Minigunner (GM) is 60 at level 5. Towers with DPS > 70, in reverse order, are (figures round to the nearest whole number): Turret: 125 Outlaw: 97 Shedder: 90 Golden Crook Boss: 80 Golden Cowboy: 73 (I copy the data from official wiki to illustrate the idea, please don’t off the focus with Robox engine issues, frame refreshing rate or whatsoever, unless you believe they invalidate my argument.) If you check other towers, you will find that DPS of Cowboy and Crook Boss (CB) at level 5 are same as GM, i.e 60. It is tempting to conclude that the 3 towers are equally powerful at max level. Is it fair? If we look closer, the range of GM is 21 while that of Cowboy and CB are both 16, about 25% lower than that of GM. That means GM can inflict more damage on zombies. It concludes that GM is in fact more powerful than the other two. Now we need a new indicator, lets call it Total Damage Index (TDI): TDI = DPS x Range. E.g. TDI of level 5 GM = 1260 TDI of level 5 Cowboy = 960 TDI of level 5 CB = 960 Towers with TDI > 1000, in reverse order, are (figures round to the nearest whole number): Outlaw: 3866 Turret: 3250 Motar: 2078 Commando: 1323 Golden Cowboy: 1320 Golden Crook Boss: 12

matches.title: why I think There is no best golden skin
matches.snippet: Small note: I lost my old account (hihihi99) so this is my new account So you probably hear of golden skins. If you haven't played tds for 2 years or something, golden skins are skins from golden crates that give buffs to towers, like damage. Every golden skin has its unique buff that differs it from the other golden skins and making it better than the original tower. However, you probably also hear of something like this: Golden minigunner is the best golden skin! or Golden soldier is the best golden skin!. Personally, I don't think there is any best golden skin, since there is no golden skin thats amazing at everything and is op from waves 1-40. For example, lets take golden minigunner. Golden minigunner might be a good mid-late game tower, but im pretty sure you can't get it on wave 1 and you will have to leak alot and maybe even die before affording it. Another example could be golden scout. It does excel at wave 1-9, but golden scout is never going to be able to handle the last waves of fallen mode unless you spam it real bad until the placement limit and then fallen king comes and wrecks you on the last wave instead. In conclusion, every golden skin is good at its own thing (yes even golden pyromancer since he can reduce defense of enemies on fallen mode) and there isn't really a best golden skin unless your talking of the best golden skin in a very specific scenario. It was most notable for adding the Lunar Overture Event. But aside from that, it came with another long list of balance changes, and finally new towers after 10 months. Let’s dive in. NEW TOWERS Necromancer - This tower was actually added 3 days later on v1.9.0g. It was unlocked from the shop with 1,800 Gems. The Necromancer was quite a complicated tower. At early levels, it fires magic bolts, which at Level 1+ , can pierce through enemies. At Level 4, this is replaced by a beam fired from its book, which are not projectiles and can hit up to 4 enemies at once. That’s not what the tower really is about though. It has a “Soul Meter” stat which it fills up by simply damaging enemies, when it becomes full, it creates a gravestone near it on the path, having a maximum of 6. It can destroy its gravestones using its “Raise the Dead” ability, which periodically stops it from attacking, these gravestones will then summon random units, and any units spawned by the previous use of the ability will be killed. At Level 4, these gravestones also explode when destroyed, dealing damage. The tower had very expensive prices, costing $45,000 to max out, and it had a placement limit of 3. At Level 0-1, it just spawns Skeletons, which just collide with enemies, having a low amount of health. At Level 1, it can now spawn Sword Skeletons, which deal melee damage. At Level 2, Skeletons are upgraded to Giant Skeletons, having way more health, and Sword Skeletons are upgraded to Skeleton Knights. At Level 3, Giant Skeletons are upgraded to Hallow Guards, and Necromancer can now summon an Executioner Skeleton, having long range, and throwing an axe to deal quick ticks of damage, which then returns after 4 seconds, and it also had a lot of health. As for the overall stats of the Necromancer, its single-target DPS was abysmal for its cost, but that doesn’t really matter, because it is able to hit multiple enemies, so even the Necromancer itself deals with hordes well. The skeletons themselves are much more powerful though when stacked, especially the Executioner Skeleton. The tower is best used for late-game since the early units are very weak. But honestly, the tower is just… unreliable. The skeletons spawned by the ability are completely random every time, and the ability also kills the previously spawned skeletons and periodically stops the Necromancer from attacking, and even then the skeletons die easily when not used right. Don’t get me wrong, the tower is fun to use, especially and can be strong when used right at max level, but it’s just not really reliable. It lands a spot on high C tier. Jester - Added on November 12th, 2023, along with Act 3, the final act of the event, with the Jester being the tower reward for beating it. It threw a bomb at enemies, which obviously dealt splash damage, and it gets two bombs at Level 4. The tower was mainly focused on debuffs, with different types of bombs providing different effects.. The first type of bomb, being the fire bomb which is unlocked at Level 0, obviously deals burn damage, and surprisingly the tower’s DPS is really good for its cost with these fire bombs, and it still deals hordes really well with its splash damage and high burn damage. At Level 2, it can now use ice bombs, which freezes affected enemies for 2 seconds, but decreases Jester’s DPS a lot. At Level 3, it can now use poison bombs, which leaves an acid puddle upon exploding that lasts for 10 seconds, and dealing damage-over-time to enemies, though its single-target DPS was really low and the bombs don’t even splash damage. At Level 4, it can now use confusion bombs, which causes enemies to walk backwards for 3 seconds, being an 8 second cooldown after for each Jester. However, the confusion bombs affected MAJOR BOSSES, such as Fallen King, Nuclear Monster, and Void Reaver, overall making the tower extremely potent with stalling and debuffing enemies. Use fire bombs for DPS, and the ice and confusion bombs for stalling (but NEVER use ice with fire now due to a new rework for the debuff system). The confusion bombs being able to affect major bosses just trivialized the game. (feels like pre-bugfix Toxic Gunner all over again).
